description.value: The study examined how behavioral inhibition and activation motivation dispositions modulate neural responses during cognitive reappraisal of emotional pictures in currently drug-free depressed outpatients compared with healthy controls.

design.value: A block-design fMRI study comparing 12 currently drug-free major depressed outpatients with 15 healthy controls during attend, detach, and immerse emotion-regulation conditions, with group, emotion, and reappraisal analyses and BIS/BAS motivation measures.

name.value: Behavioral Inhibition System and Behavioral Activation System Scale (BBS)

description.value: A revised Chinese version of the scale, with BIS, BASR, BASD, and BASF subscales, administered immediately after the scan.
A 21-item self-rating scale measuring emotional, cognitive, motivational, and somatic symptoms, scored from 0 to 3.
A 20-item scale assessing psychological and somatic symptoms, scored from 1 to 4.
An interview scale used to measure severity of depression.
Participants rated emotional intensity on a 4-point Likert scale.

task_description.value: Participants performed three consecutive blocks: ATTEND, DETACH, and IMMERSE. Attend required responding naturally without changing the emotional state; detach required interpreting the situation as fake or unreal; immerse required perceiving each picture as real by imagining oneself or a loved one in the scene.

instructions.value: Attend naturally without trying to change the emotional state; detach by interpreting the situation as fake or unreal; immerse by perceiving each picture as real and imagining oneself or a loved one in the scene.

stimuli.value: Affective pictures selected from the International Affective Picture System; positive, negative, and neutral pictures, with neutral pictures only presented under attend.

task_performance_measures.value: self-reported ratings of emotional intensity on a 4-point Likert scale

instrument.value: Siemens 3T Tim Trio MRI system (Erlangen, Germany)

description.value: Three functional sessions were acquired. Functional sequence had a flip angle of 90°, FOV of 240 × 240 mm2, matrix of 64 × 64, slice thickness of 4 mm, and slice interval of 0.8 mm. Visual stimuli were presented through goggles mounted on the head coil.

The first trial of each block was discarded to reach magnetization equilibrium. Remaining volumes were slice-time corrected, realigned to the mean volume, spatially normalized to standard MNI space, and smoothed with an 8-mm FWHM isotropic Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: Discard the first trial of each block
Realignment to the mean volume to correct for head motion
Spatial normalization to standard MNI space using a 12-parameter affine transformation
Smoothing with an 8-mm full-width at half-maximum isotropic Gaussian kernel

model_settings.value: Each condition was modeled using a box-car function convolved with a canonical HRF. Realignment parameters were included as covariates of no interest. Whole-brain voxel-wise analyses, ANCOVA, one-sample t-tests, two-sample t-tests, and generalized linear regression models were used.

estimator.value: multiple linear regression, ANCOVA, one-sample t-test, two-sample t-test, and generalized linear regression

model_type.value: independent sample t-tests and multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA)

model_settings.value: BBS subscale scores were compared between groups; MANOVA tested effects of group and/or gender. Outliers over 3 standard deviations were diagnosed and excluded, using box-plot methods and Cook's distance.

description.value: Subjects responded naturally without trying to change the emotional state elicited by the stimuli; this was the baseline condition.
Avoidance-oriented reappraisal in which participants interpreted the depicted situation as fake or unreal, as would someone with no personal attachment to the events.
Approach-oriented reappraisal in which subjects perceived each picture as real by imagining themselves or a loved one in the scene.
Positive emotional pictures.
Negative emotional pictures.
Neutral pictures, presented only under the attend condition.

title.value: Motivational dispositions Predict Reappraisal-related Brain Activity in functional ROIs.

footer.value: BIS/BAS scores were entered into a generalized linear regression model to predict reappraisal-related brain activation. Functional ROI time courses (beta values) under each condition in each group were generated by extracting the first eigenvariate of 8 mm around the peak voxels of respective clusters with no scaling, using a Matlab package REX.
